findings.explanation: Splunkbase 1352 is the "App for Cisco Network Data" (cisco_ios), an app for Cisco IOS, NX-OS and WLC dashboards. It is not a "Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security", and it has nothing to do with Cisco Spaces asset tracking.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove this reference. If you need a second source, use Cisco Spaces IoT Explorer or Firehose API documentation.

findings.explanation: This is the generic Cisco security product support index, which does not cover Cisco Spaces, BLE tags or geofencing. The HEC reference is also unrelated, because the Spaces add-on uses a modular Firehose input, not HEC.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace these with Cisco Spaces documentation for IoT Explorer asset tracking and the Firehose API (event types DEVICE_LOCATION_UPDATE and IOT_TELEMETRY).

findings.explanation: In `implementation`, the assignment lookup, the asset_value tiers, the 30-minute dwell outside the zone and the business-hours restriction all describe logic that is absent from `spl`. The SPL never calls a lookup, reads `assignedZone` straight from the event, alerts at once on any mismatch, and applies the 3600-second check at all hours.
findings.quote: Maintain a lookup table of asset assignments (asset_tag, assigned_zone, asset_category, asset_value). Alert immediately on high-value assets leaving their zone. For lower-value assets, alert after 30 minutes outside zone. Track "last seen" timestamps and flag assets not seen for >1 hour during business hours.
findings.suggested_fix: Either rewrite the implementation to describe exactly what the SPL does, or record that the SPL needs a `lookup` on assetTag for assigned_zone and asset_value, plus duration and business-hours logic. A human must make that SPL change.

findings.explanation: The data sources name neither the index nor the sourcetype the SPL uses (`cisco_spaces` / `cisco:spaces:assets`). They also do not explain how the nested Firehose JSON becomes the flat fields `assetName`, `assetTag`, `assetCategory`, `currentZone`, `assignedZone` and `lastSeenTime`. As written, a reader cannot tell whether those fields come from the add-on, from custom props.conf work, or from a lookup.
findings.quote: Cisco Spaces Firehose API (IOT_TELEMETRY, DEVICE_LOCATION_UPDATE events for BLE tags)
findings.suggested_fix: State the index and sourcetype the Spaces add-on writes. Name the Firehose JSON paths each SPL field is derived from, and say which fields (assignedZone, asset category) come from a customer-maintained lookup.

findings.explanation: The Cisco Spaces Firehose has a dedicated ASSET_LOCATION_UPDATE event type for asset locator devices (BLE, RFID, UWB). It carries assetInfo.id, category, department and position.lastLocatedTime. DEVICE_LOCATION_UPDATE covers Wi-Fi client devices, and IOT_TELEMETRY covers sensor readings such as temperature and battery.
findings.quote: IOT_TELEMETRY, DEVICE_LOCATION_UPDATE events for BLE tags
findings.suggested_fix: Name ASSET_LOCATION_UPDATE as the primary event type for tracking tagged assets, and map assetName/assetTag/assetCategory/lastSeenTime to the assetLocationUpdate.assetInfo.* and position.lastLocatedTime JSON paths.

findings.explanation: The validation step points to a building management system (BMS) console. The source of truth for BLE tag location and geofences is Cisco Spaces IoT Explorer. The step also truncates the implementation text mid-sentence ("Generate weekly…") and repeats "Step 4 — Operationalize" four times.
findings.quote:
Step 3 — Validate
Compare with the BMS console for the same equipment, sensors, and time range.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate by comparing a flagged asset's zone and last-seen time with its entry in Cisco Spaces IoT Explorer for the same window. Remove the duplicated Step 4 headings and the truncation.

findings.explanation: On Splunkbase, the current Spaces Add-On release (2.0.20) lists Splunk platform compatibility as 9.4 through 10.6, not 9.2.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the value to 9.4+ (and Cloud), matching the add-on compatibility on Splunkbase.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The per-event fields `zone_violation` and `missing` are not carried through `stats ... by assetName, assetTag, assetCategory`, because stats drops any field that is not aggregated or in the by-clause. As a result, the later `eval status=case(isnotnull(zone_violation), ..., isnotnull(missing), ..., 1==1, "Unknown")` labels every row "Unknown", and the GEOFENCE ALERT / MISSING split never works. Aggregate the flags inside stats, for example `values(zone_violation) as zone_violation, values(missing) as missing`.

`sourcetype="cisco:spaces:assets"` does not appear to be a sourcetype that the Spaces Add-On for Splunk (ta_cisco_spaces, Splunkbase 8485) produces. A published setup skill that inspected the package lists only `cisco:spaces:firehose`, `cisco:spaces:firehose:health` and `cisco:spaces:log`, with all Firehose event types under `cisco:spaces:firehose`. Check props.conf in the add-on; if it confirms this, rescope the search to `sourcetype=cisco:spaces:firehose` filtered on the Firehose event type, and map the nested JSON paths to the fields used. Evidence: https://www.skillsdirectory.com/skills/chambear2809-cisco-spaces-setup

The missing-asset branch (`_time-lastSeenTime>3600`) only fires when an event arrives for an asset whose own lastSeenTime is stale. An asset that has stopped reporting produces no new Firehose events, so a search over streamed location updates will not detect it. Detecting absence needs a comparison of latest(_time) per assetTag against an asset inventory lookup.

summary: The implementation prose describes a plausible BLE asset-tracking workflow, but it does not match the SPL. The SPL has a logic bug that makes every row come out as "Unknown", it relies on a sourcetype and flat fields that the Spaces add-on does not appear to produce, and the references cite an unrelated Splunkbase app under the wrong name.
